title: Usage Insights (Route + Model) — Kickoff Working Notes
content:
Doc purpose
Working notes from the initial engineering + product kickoff for “In-console usage insights” (route + model cost/usage breakdown, top drivers, exports, and correctness vs billing). This is not a PRD; it’s the capture of decisions, open questions, and who owns what.

Meeting
Date: 2026-01-08 (Thu)
Duration: 60 min
Location: Zoom + #eng-platform / #product follow-ups
Facilitator: Dylan Brooks
Note taker: Chloe Martin

Attendees
Product
- Marissa Cole (Product lead, Console insights)
- Paula Mendes (PM partner, rollout)

Engineering
- Dylan Brooks (Eng lead, Console & Tooling)
- Chloe Martin (Console backend lead)
- Logan Wright (Telemetry & analytics platform lead)
- Nadia Rahman (Cost attribution pipeline owner)
- Cole Summers (Billing hooks & totals correctness)
- Kaitlyn Nguyen (AuthN/AuthZ, RBAC enforcement)
- Allison Grant (Observability quality reviewer)

Design / DX / Docs
- Tessa Morgan (Design lead)
- Alex Martinez (DevEx lead)
- Elliot Price (Docs lead)

Context / why now
- Customers increasingly ask for spend breakdown by API route + model (and the “what changed?” delta explanation) so engineering can action it and finance can reconcile.
- We have partial telemetry today (tokens in/out, model, workspace/project) but route attribution is inconsistent, and model aliases create noisy grouping.
- We must ensure totals align with billing totals (or clearly communicate drift and freshness) before broad rollout.

Goals (Phase 0–1)
1) Deliver interactive console table: cost + usage breakdown by route + model with filters (time range, workspace/project, env, region if available).
2) Ensure consistent semantics for route grouping (normalization), model bucketing (family/version), and attribution across fallbacks/retries.
3) Add export (CSV) that matches the console totals and is reconcilable to invoice totals (within agreed tolerance + documented reasons when not exact).
4) Add data freshness indicators and guardrails for cardinality + query latency.

Non-goals (initial)
- Auto-apply optimization actions (we only link to recommended levers/docs)
- Scheduled email reports
- Customer-defined arbitrary dimensions

Current state snapshot (as discussed)
Telemetry sources
- Metering events include: workspace_id, project_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency buckets; route field exists in gateway logs but not reliably present in metering stream for all endpoints/regions.
- Retries exist at multiple layers (client retry vs gateway retry vs backend retry). Today attribution in billing uses “billed tokens” after successful completion, with special handling for certain failure cases.

Known pain points
- Route cardinality risk: untemplated paths (/v1/projects/12345/…) will explode group-by unless normalized.
- Model identity: model aliases (marketing names) vs internal ids create duplicate rows.
- Streaming: token_out can be final vs incremental; we need a consistent “billable token_out” for reports.
- Fallbacks: when routing policy falls back to a different model, we must decide whether to attribute cost to requested model or actual served model.

Key decisions (tentative, needs ADR)
1) Primary grouping keys (v1)
- Workspace + project (required)
- Time bucket: hourly for <= 7d ranges, daily for > 7d ranges (subject to perf)
- Route: normalized/canonicalized route template (see open questions)
- Model: “served_model_family + served_model_version” (plus model_id raw for debug)

2) Attribution model
- Attribute cost and usage to the actual served model (not requested model), but keep requested_model fields for drilldown and “fallback rate” driver.
- Retries: count “attempts” and “retry_count” as separate metrics; billed cost should align to billing’s successful completion rules (Cole to confirm exact edge cases).

3) Console totals vs billing
- Console should match billing totals for the same workspace/time window within a defined tolerance. If it can’t (late events / backfill), the UI must show freshness/lag and “partial data” banner.

4) Cardinality guardrails
- Route dimension must enforce:
  - templating of common identifiers (UUIDs, numeric ids, hashes) to placeholders
  - a max distinct routes per workspace per day (soft limit with warnings; hard limit for export)
  - “Other / Unattributed” bucket for unknown/unnormalized routes

Open questions / risks
A) Route normalization (ENG-3813)
- What is the canonical route string for OpenAI-compatible endpoints? (e.g., /v1/chat/completions vs /openai/v1/chat/completions)
- Do we normalize method+path or path-only? (likely include method to reduce ambiguity; design wants “endpoint” display names)
- How do we handle customer-proxied routes or custom gateways? (likely “unknown” bucket + docs)
- What is the fallback when the route tag is missing? (unattributed bucket + count missing_route_tag)

B) Model bucketing (ENG-3823)
- How to handle versionless aliases (e.g., “llama-3.1-70b” pointing to patch versions)?
- Do we show “family” and “version” columns separately in export? (finance prefers stable “family” and separate “variant” column)

C) Billing correctness + time alignment (ENG-3817)
- Timezone: billing is UTC; console default timezone is user locale. Proposed: queries always use UTC boundaries under the hood; UI displays local but explicitly labels.
- Rounding policy: per-row rounding vs post-aggregation rounding can cause drift in exports.
- Late events: what’s the maximum expected delay by region? What do we commit to for “data is final” watermark?

D) Streaming semantics
- Ensure tokens_out is finalized tokens emitted, not “best effort” partial when client disconnects.
- If client disconnects mid-stream, are tokens billed? (Cole to confirm; must reflect in report semantics.)

E) Performance
- 30-day range queries have a risk of timeouts. Mitigation: pre-aggregation + caching + limiting “top N routes/models” with pagination.

F) Permissions (ENG-3820)
- Some workspaces want usage visibility but not cost visibility. We need a “hide cost” workspace setting and role-based checks.
- Export permissions: likely restricted to billing admins / owners; audit logging required for every export download.

Initial milestones (proposed)
Phase 0: Discovery + data audit (1–2 weeks)
- Audit telemetry fields and gaps; confirm route tag availability by endpoint + region
- Draft ADR for route normalization + attribution semantics
Owners:
- Data audit: Nadia Rahman + Logan Wright
- ADR drafting: Chloe Martin (primary), Dylan Brooks (review), Cole Summers (billing semantics), Allison Grant (quality)

Phase 1: Aggregation + API + initial console table (2–4 weeks)
- Implement aggregated dataset keyed by workspace/project/time_bucket/route/model
- Build query API for breakdown table + filters
- Console: route+model table with drilldowns; basic empty states; limited range
Owners:
- Dataset/job: Logan Wright + Mei Lin (support)
- API endpoints: Chloe Martin
- Console UI: Dylan Brooks + Nora Ahmed
- Perf review: Thomas Baird

Phase 2: Top drivers + export + permissions + hardening (2–3 weeks)
- Compute “top cost drivers” + “what changed” deltas
- CSV export: async job, signed URLs, throttles/limits
- RBAC gating for cost + export; audit logs
Owners:
- Drivers service: Nadia Rahman
- Export: Chloe Martin + Felix Schneider
- RBAC + audit: Kaitlyn Nguyen + Kevin Osei
- Billing reconciliation suite: Cole Summers

Phase 3: Beta rollout + correctness validation + docs (1–2 weeks)
- Feature flag + allowlist
- Validate totals vs billing for beta customers; handle incidents/rollbacks
- Publish docs + tooltips; capture feedback loop
Owners:
- Rollout/flagging: Connor O'Brien (release) + Dylan Brooks
- Correctness validation: Cole Summers + Allison Grant
- Docs + help center: Elliot Price + Wei Chen
- DX messaging: Alex Martinez

Action items (from kickoff)
1) Telemetry gap report: identify endpoints/regions missing route tags; propose instrumentation rollout plan.
- Owner: Logan Wright
- Due: 2026-01-13

2) Draft ADR outline: route normalization rules + “unattributed” handling + examples.
- Owner: Chloe Martin
- Due: 2026-01-15

3) Billing alignment notes: document billing’s rules for retries, disconnects during streaming, and fallbacks.
- Owner: Cole Summers
- Due: 2026-01-16

4) UX table requirements: confirm column set, naming (“route” vs “endpoint”), and drilldown path.
- Owner: Tessa Morgan + Dylan Brooks
- Due: 2026-01-14

5) Permissions matrix: define roles who can see cost, see usage-only, and export; include restricted workspace behavior.
- Owner: Kaitlyn Nguyen + Naomi Feldman (to be looped)
- Due: 2026-01-17

Notes / discussion highlights
- Naming: DevEx preference is to use “Endpoint” in UI copy while keeping “route” as technical term in API/docs. Proposal: UI label “Endpoint (Route)” in early beta + tooltip.
- Finance use case: Rishi asked for “stable keys” and consistent totals to invoice. Export should include both model_family and model_version columns; also include currency + cost_usd with explicit rounding rules.
- Observability: Allison emphasized that “freshness” must be first-class to avoid misleading conclusions during lag/backfill periods.

Parking lot
- Shareable reports (link-based) in beta vs GA
- PDF export (requested by CS for QBRs) — not in initial scope
- Multi-workspace rollups for org-level admins

Next check-in
- 2026-01-15: review ADR draft + data audit results; lock v1 schema fields; confirm beta criteria + initial allowlist candidates.
